subject: sociology
title: Crime, Deviance and the Rules
welcome_lead: What makes an act criminal or just deviant? Start with the basics that every later study builds.
meta_desc: GCSE Sociology adventure introducing crime, deviance, social control and Durkheim's view on crime.
final_note: Deviance bends rules. Crime breaks laws. Knowing the difference is the first exam mark.

concepts.def: An act that breaks the formal law of the land.
Behaviour that breaks social norms but not law.
Ways society pressures people to follow rules.
Written rules enforced by police, courts, schools.
Family, peers and gossip shaping behaviour.

walkthroughs.body_html: Talking loudly on the bus is deviant but legal. Speeding is criminal but barely seen as deviant. Some acts (murder) are both. Some acts (eating with hands) are deviant in one culture, normal in another.

Durkheim argued a small amount of crime is healthy. It reinforces shared values when offenders are punished, allows change (yesterday's criminals are today's heroes), and acts as a warning of social problems.
Formal control = police, courts, prisons, school sanctions. Informal control = parents' disapproval, friends' teasing, religious guilt. Both push people to conform.
